stemBlocks.value: The time t varies inversely as the speed v. If t = 5 hours when v = 60 km/h, find t when v = 75 km/h.
Think first: Time and speed multiply to give a fixed distance, so find that distance first.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p118-q14 from workbook page 118.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the variation statement as an equation.
Substitute t = 5 and v = 60 to find k.

strategyBlocks.value: Write t = k/v, find k from t = 5 and v = 60, then substitute v = 75.

whyThisWorks.value: The constant 300 is the distance travelled, unchanged by how fast you go. Raising the speed from 60 to 75 km/h is multiplying by 5/4, so the time is multiplied by 4/5 — five hours becomes four.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding time because the speed increased.
